note: Source "though it may be in my power" is a hedge; candidate asserts "I am free".
replacement: 5. What I find most important here is this. I discover in my mind countless ideas of certain objects. These cannot be counted as pure negations, although perhaps they have no reality beyond my thought. I did not make them up, even though it may be in my power to think of them or not. They have true and immutable natures of their own. Take the example of a triangle. Perhaps there is not, and never was, any such figure anywhere in the universe outside my thought. Still, it remains true that this figure has a certain determinate nature, form or essence, which is immutable and eternal, was not made up by me, and does not depend at all on my thought. This is clear from the fact that many properties of the triangle can be demonstrated: that its three angles are equal to two right angles, that its greatest side is opposite its greatest angle, and the like. Whether I wish it or not, I now clearly discern that these belong to the triangle, although I did not think of them at all when I first imagined it. So it cannot be said that I invented them.
